inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL INSERT IGNORE selects a bounded source subset into a target table so duplicate-key rows are skipped while the selected non-conflicting rows are loaded.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a catalog-feed load with an explicit priority and primary-key tie-breaker. INSERT IGNORE ... SELECT uses ORDER BY and LIMIT to select the top three feed rows; one selected row conflicts with an existing catalog key and is ignored, while the other selected rows are inserted. The source schema, names, and values are newly authored.

fixture_notes: The feed ranks SKU 30 first, SKU 20 second, SKU 10 third, and SKU 40 fourth. SKU 10 already exists in the live catalog, so the LIMIT 3 source subset still inserts only SKUs 30 and 20; SKU 10 remains unchanged and SKU 40 is not selected.
determinism_notes: Priority descending plus unique SKU ascending defines the selected source subset. All values are fixed and there are no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections.
setup: CREATE TABLE catalog_feed (sku INT PRIMARY KEY, label VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, priority INT NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE live_catalog (sku INT PRIMARY KEY, label VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, priority INT NOT NULL)

steps.sql: INSERT IGNORE INTO live_catalog (sku, label, priority) SELECT sku, label, priority FROM catalog_feed ORDER BY priority DESC, sku LIMIT 3

checks.sql: SELECT sku, label, priority FROM live_catalog ORDER BY sku
SELECT sku, label, priority FROM catalog_feed ORDER BY sku
